title: Long-Tenancy Carpet Wear Allowance on the Security Deposit Account
content:
**Term.** A long tenancy earns a wear allowance on the Security Deposit Account. The allowance is a share of the corrected carpet charge that is not charged.

- **0.12 (12 percent)** for a tenancy of at least 48 full months from the lease's move-in date to its move-out date, with no late fee posted on the lease fewer than twenty-four full months before the handling date.
- **0.08 (8 percent)** for a tenancy of at least 48 full months with exactly one late fee posted in those twenty-four months.
- **None** for any other tenancy.

The corrected carpet charge is reduced by the wear allowance, and it is rounded half up to the cent once, at the end.

**Records read.** From the Apartment Home Lease: the move-in date, and the late fees posted on the lease ledger with their dates. From the deposit account: the move-out date.

## Ladder

| Full months, move-in to move-out | Late fees on the lease in the 24 months before the handling date | Wear allowance |
|---|---|---|
| 48 or more | none | 0.12 |
| 48 or more | exactly one | 0.08 |
| 48 or more | two or more | none |
| fewer than 48 | any | none |

## Hypothetical cases

- A tenancy of 52 full months with no late fees in the 24 months, and a carpet charge before the allowance of 400.00 USD: the charge is reduced by 0.12, to 352.00 USD.
- A tenancy of 47 full months with a spotless record: no allowance.
- One late fee posted 30 months before the handling date falls outside the twenty-four months.
